name: Gene Karpinski, LCV
subject: URGENT: Government shutdown is imminent and House GOP won't stop attacking the environment
body:
__Bottom line, your contribution goes further to win environmental campaigns that matter if you give now. |
---

|
**Peter, the deadline to fund the government is TOMORROW.** Republicans are using the opportunity to ram through a dangerous, polluter-driven agenda to:
* Drop EPA funding to its lowest levels in more than 30 years
* Slash clean air protections
* Mandate dirty energy lease sales
* Cut critical environmental clean-up programs

_... and they're bringing us to the brink of another government shutdown to get their way._

**We need a major show of strength from the environmental movement** to ensure that Congress doesn't cut critical environmental protections during last-minute negotiations.

**We have just hours to make a difference.** [The best thing you can do right now is renew your LCV membership to power our campaigns. Even $5 will have an impact. A group of donors is triple matching every gift through the end of the month -- that means whatever you give today will be TRIPLED.](https://links.messages.lcv.)

Peter -- I really hope you'll take this opportunity to triple your impact -- because as urgent as these budget negotiations are, it's not the only environmental fight we're up against. There are so many reasons to pitch in -- because there are so many ways your support will make a difference. Here are just a few:
1. **Because the Biden administration released a final plan for offshore drilling** and is considering additional protections for public lands and waters. Fossil fuel extraction on public lands generates a quarter of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions. [This could be HUGE, but only if the environmental movement shows up >>](https://links.messages.lcv.)
2. **Because Republicans are threatening our voting rights** -- and the newly-reintroduced John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act could be the most significant federal voting reform bill since the Voting Rights Act. The ONLY way this passes Congress is with a major grassroots push. [Your support defends the freedom to vote. Donate today >>](https://links.messages.lcv.)
3. **Because LCV is pressuring the Biden administration to finalize the strongest possible fuel efficiency standards** for clean cars in order to protect our communities from pollution and drive the clean energy transition. [Your support makes that happen. Donate today >>](https://links.messages.lcv.)
4. **Because a group of donors is triple-matching every contribution this month.** Bottom line, your contribution goes further to win environmental campaigns that matter if you give now. [Renew your LCV membership for $5 and triple your impact today >>](https://links.messages.lcv.)

We need to go all out right now -- to win each and every one of these fights. But it's only going to happen if the environmental movement shows up during the moments that matter most.

**Thank you, thank you, thank you for everything that you do for the environment, Peter.**

Onward,

Gene Karpinski
President
League of Conservation Voters ____ |

name: Courier Newsroom
subject: MSM coverage of Trump: what’s covered vs. what’s omitted
body:
# [](https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/83?t=1&akid=1645%2E120351%2Esw1tSr)
Peter,
Donald Trump is masterful at exploiting the mainstream media’s flaws to spread conspiracy theories, lies, and hate.
Of those flaws, the media’s commitment to telling “both sides” of a political story has been the easiest to exploit. Trump won the White House in 2016 by spreading endless lies about Hillary Clinton, knowing full well that the media would take the bait.
**[Before we talk about how Courier is working to fight back against that dynamic ahead of the 2024 presidential race, can you pitch in $5 or anything you can right now ahead of our end-of-quarter deadline? Your support will allow our talented news teams to tell the whole truth about Donald Trump in key battleground states nationwide.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-courier-20230929?refcode=em20230929&amount=5&refcode2=1645_120351_sw1tSr&akid=1645%2E120351%2Esw1tSr)**
This week, Trump and President Biden held dueling events in Michigan — ostensibly in support of striking UAW autoworkers.
President Biden became the first president to picket alongside striking workers. Meanwhile, Trump staged a sham photo op at a nonunion factory, giving a campaign speech filled with lies and hallucinations about his previous record of supporting workers.
The truth, of course is that Donald Trump’s administration was one of the most hostile to unions in our nation’s history. Under the Trump administration, auto manufacturing jobs fell. Trump once proposed gutting the auto industry in Michigan and moving the jobs to states where workers aren’t paid a fair wage.
**So how did mainstream outlets do in covering Trump’s speech, Peter? Spoiler alert: not good!**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-courier-20230929?refcode=em20230929&amount=5&refcode2=1645_120351_sw1tSr&akid=1645%2E120351%2Esw1tSr)
Rather than calling out Trump’s blatant lies and history of hostility towards Michigan’s workforce, the mainstream media focused on the so-called “horse race,” framing the dueling campaign stops as a contest to win working-class voters in Michigan.
On the other hand, here’s what coverage looked like in our Michigan newsroom, _The Gander:_
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-courier-20230929?refcode=em20230929&amount=5&refcode2=1645_120351_sw1tSr&akid=1645%2E120351%2Esw1tSr)
At Courier, our network of local newsrooms nationwide is dedicated to telling audiences the whole truth, no matter what. **We will never compromise our values or back down from right-wing efforts to use the media to spread lies and hate.**
But to continue doing this important work, we’ll need to continue to amass the resources necessary to counter right-wing misinformation campaigns and the bad actors who knowingly spread them.

I came to this country as a 14-year-old immigrant from Ecuador. My family lived in a one-room apartment, and my mom worked double shifts to pay the bills. I got a job at the local doughnut shop to help her make ends meet.
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/70630438/429922593/-225452087?refcode=BLU-FFP-20230929-1-EM&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNS8xLzc3NDA2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjcyNDVkNDAwLTBiNWYtZWUxMS05OTM3LTAwMjI0ODMyZWI3MyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=P20XKmY4bhi4hnxfc9V7JOfvvsZe1Flwp-N2gf7kbhM=)
I’ve seen firsthand just how difficult it is for working families to get by. **But I’ve also seen the incredible opportunities that are only possible in America.**

I was able to attend college, give back to my community, and become the first South American immigrant ever elected to Congress. And, after years of long shifts and late-night classes to learn English, my mom was able to retire with dignity thanks to Social Security and Medicare.

Make no mistake: There’s a lot of work that we have to do to make sure that every family has the chance to achieve their American Dream. That’s why I’m running for Senate — to protect and expand the opportunities that made my story possible.

I’m running against Rick Scott, who’s spent his career attacking those opportunities and threatening vital programs like Social Security and Medicare. He has a personal fortune of up to a quarter of a billion dollars to fund his campaign. That’s why I’m counting on a grassroots army made up of people like you to fight back.

The Vote To Live Campaign has been working day in and day out since 2016 to ensure that every Black voter is registered and ready to vote.

**Now, we’re taking it to the next level and helping those voters actually cast their ballots.**

Ritchie Torres represents the future of the Democratic Party. Raised by a single mother in public housing, Ritchie personally understands the hardships that working families endure. At age 25, Ritchie made history as the youngest elected official to serve on the New York City Council. He fought tirelessly for the working families of The Bronx, and now, he's fighting for those families and for progressive values in Congress. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: This is a chance for you to show that you’re still in this fight
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
We can fight back against powerful interests like the gun lobby, Big Pharma, and fossil fuel giants who've used their deep pockets to block the change we’re fighting to make.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=90%2E4032634%2EFVYNKe)
---
I'm deeply grateful for every grassroots donor who chips in to help power our movement — because funding our campaign from the grassroots level makes a powerfully important difference. Over time, a democracy with political campaigns funded by a small number of people who can contribute a lot of money looks very different from a democracy with campaigns funded by a large number of people who chip in a little at a time. It’s the difference between a government that works great for those at the top and a government that can work for everyone. With a grassroots-funded movement, we can fight back against powerful interests like the gun lobby, Big Pharma, and fossil fuel giants who've used their deep pockets to block the change we’re fighting to make. And every three months, when we publish our fundraising numbers after the quarterly FEC deadline, we get a chance to show that grassroots donors like you are still in this fight. [**If you’re able to, will you pitch in $28 or whatever makes sense by tomorrow's important deadline? Your donation will support my re-election campaign and keep up the fight for creating universal child care, passing a wealth tax, getting corruption out of our government, and much more.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/651?amount=28&t=8&akid=90%2E4032634%2EFVYNKe) We need to defend and expand our Senate majority, retake the House, and re-elect Joe Biden and Kamala Harris in 2024 — because everything we’re fighting for would be a whole lot easier if we had more champions for working people in office. And our chances of making big, structural change all come screeching to a halt if Republicans take any more power. Democrats win when we go out there and fight for the bold action that families need. But winning majorities is not enough. We need to use those majorities to pass plans that truly transform the lives of working people in this country. So I’m fighting my heart out to get as much done as possible with the Congress we have now. And I’m working to elect more Democrats up and down the ballot so we can expand our majorities and get more of our plans on the table. [**Will you chip in $28 or anything you can to make sure I can continue this work in the Senate? I’m fighting to keep making progress NOW — and I’ve got a whole bunch of plans for what we can accomplish with a Democratic House, a Democratic Senate, and a Democratic White House in 2025. Your support makes this work possible.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/651?amount=28&t=9&akid=90%2E4032634%2EFVYNKe) I never expect you to donate to every email, and I’m grateful for your support no matter what. If a financial contribution would make sense for you right now, it would be a huge help. Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth

Peter,

Fellow conservative,

I’m going to be as frank with you as I possibly can.

Because the truth is we didn’t make history last year because of any of those things. **We made history because working folks just like you – teachers, nurses, service workers, accountants, retirees, students – believed in a better future for our children.** And even in the face of massive outside spending, our team got the job done – which might have surprised the outsiders, _but I always knew our people-powered team would be able to rise to the occasion._

**Now, I’m calling on our grassroots team to step up again.** As you know, our 2024 race is incredibly competitive and the implications of what happens in our race stretch far beyond Southwest Ohio. If we are able to keep OH-01 blue, we will have the ability to tip the balance of power in the House and ensure Congress can deliver the results that children and families deserve.

**And that work starts right here, right now, with our end-of-quarter deadline.**

**I believe in our campaign more than anything. Always have, and always will. And I know we have what it takes to win again — but only if we do this together. That’s why I’m personally asking each and everyone of you:

_Greg_

Pearson, joined their urgent calls for gun safety reform. = Photo credit: Ray Di Pietro That’s because Gloria’s not afraid to do what’s right, even when it isn’t easy. In Washington, she won’t be beholden to special interests or party leaders. She will listen to us — and she won’t hesitate to fight on our behalf. = | = When Gloria was a child, her parents never hesitated to help kids, neighbors, and friends who needed a hand. Gloria is carrying on their legacy — first as a special education teacher and now as a representative. So even though she knows this won’t be an easy race to win, when Gloria saw that Tennesseans needed her to step up, she didn’t hesitate. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thanks so much, Team G | Gloria Johnson is running for the U.S. Senate because Tennesseans deserve leaders who care. body:
I took to the streets as part of the Ferguson Uprising, and I bring that bold vision for justice with me to Congress. | |
---
Peter, After a police officer killed Michael Brown, I took to the streets for over 400 days as part of the Ferguson Uprising. That multiracial movement was a pivotal point in the centuries-long struggle for Black liberation in our country, and it transformed what we thought was possible for our communities. **I bring that transformative vision to my service in Congress** , where I’ve introduced groundbreaking policies to heal the harms of generations of anti-Black criminalization and police violence, and invest in the resources Black communities need after centuries of exploitation and disinvestment. The first Black woman to serve Missouri in Congress, **I’ve personally experienced systemic racism in education, healthcare, housing, the workplace, and at the hands (and boots) of police.** I don’t want anyone else to have to go through what I’ve gone through. That’s why I lead with love for all. I don’t take any money from corporate PACs, making sure our movement for transformative change is people-powered. And right now we’re up against the urgent end of the quarter fundraising deadline. To return to Congress and continue to be the bold leader our communities need, we have to demonstrate our power now. Growing up in St. Louis, I lived through a malicious drug war that saw Black people disproportionately arrested for possession, even though usage rates for drugs like marijuana are similar.
I saw Black renters disproportionately vulnerable to eviction, and I know the policy violence of being forced out on the streets and of living out of my car with my two babies.
As a nurse and a patient with traumatic birthing experiences, I’ve seen how Black women die every day because our healthcare system denies our humanity. And while serving people with mental health crises and substance use disorders, I witnessed punitive responses that criminalized and harmed vulnerable people.
**These lived experiences fuel my urgency and bold leadership in Congress.**
That’s why I’ve led on preventing evictions and passing expansive policies, such as the _Drug Policy Reform Act_ , which would **end criminal penalties for drug use and replace them with health-centered approaches**. The bill would also expunge existing records and eliminate many of the life-long consequences associated with drug arrests and convictions: the denial of employment, housing, public benefits, drivers’ licenses, and voting rights.
I’ve also led policies like the _People’s Response Act_ , which would **invest in public health alternatives** to policing and transform our racist systems of “public safety” to center care and compassion rather than criminalization and punishment.
**I’m continuing the push for reparations** for the descendants of enslaved Black people who built this country’s wealth. And I’m championing the Equal Rights Amendment, which is **an essential tool to achieve reproductive justice and eliminate wealth and health gaps rooted in racism and misogyny.**
**Together, we have the power to bring about the change our lives depend on. But to stand up to the powerful perpetrators of injustice, we need financial support.**

name: Mike Thompson
subject: Remembering Dianne Feinstein
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mike Thompson For Congress unsubscribe: https://support
body:
# [#]
Peter,

This morning, we learned of the passing of Senator Dianne Feinstein.

Senator Feinstein was a legendary public servant, and an unmatched champion for California and our nation. She put the entirety of her heart and soul into serving the communities she loved. California, and the nation as a whole, owe her a debt of gratitude.

Dianne broke many glass ceilings. From serving as the first female president of the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, the first female mayor of San Francisco, to the first female senator from our state. She was a trailblazer in every meaning of the word.

Dianne held the love and trust of her constituents and her colleagues because of her tremendous work ethic, deep knowledge of issues, and her willingness to work across the aisle to get things done. As chair of the Senate Judiciary Committee and Intelligence Committee, she tirelessly fought for our country, no matter how difficult the challenge or complex the issue.

Dianne and I worked closely together on projects that have improved the lives of the people of our state, particularly on the Northern California Coastal Wild Heritage Wilderness Act that protected hundreds of thousands of acres and will ensure these pristine lands and opportunities for outdoor recreation will be enjoyed for generations to come.

She was a champion for gun violence prevention issues and was a tireless advocate for keeping our communities safe. Her legacy will never be forgotten.

Dianne Feinstein was my friend, an outstanding public servant, and her voice and advocacy will be sorely missed. Jan and I send our thoughts and prayers to her friends, family, and staff during this sad time.

May her memory be a blessing.

Best,

Mike Thompson

The landscape for reproductive rights continues to shift, and we have to stay light on our feet to respond. Currently, 12 states have enacted near-total bans on abortion, and another 7 states have either significant restrictions or limited availability. However, our achievements last November showcased the power of the electorate: we successfully defended access to abortion in 5 different ballot measures during the 2022 midterm elections. That's evidence that when voters have a say, they choose to protect their reproductive freedoms.
**But right now, we're standing at a crossroads: Either we passively watch as extremist lawmakers continue to chip away at abortion access, or we can take decisive action.**
We've identified states where ballot measures have the potential to either restore or permanently secure access to abortion. # [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/70635539/429940309/-1695430967?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDU2NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOWI3ZTM2YzYtMWI1Zi1lZTExLTk5MzctMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Qiw_WxlBH2rwt-ABdl9UToX43ooiXRvJL4UHi5rxBFk=)
Dear Peter,

I was saddened to hear of the passing of Senator Dianne Feinstein. When Senator Feinstein was first elected in 1992, women were not allowed to wear trousers on the Senate floor, and women’s bathrooms had just been installed. Even just 31 years ago, women’s equality and women’s representation in the U.S. federal government were still just beginning.

I am grateful for her trailblazing work on behalf of Californians, and her unwavering commitment to advancing women’s rights. _Her leadership and accomplishments paved the way for many of us, and I am proud to be following in her footsteps as a woman running for office._

Today, at a time when abortion rights and the ability for women to determine their own futures has been put at risk nationwide by a Republican Congress, **women make up less than 30% of the voting members of either the Senate or the House.**

We cannot go back to a time when women’s voices are overlooked and diminished.

We cannot go back to a time when women and working families were unable to determine their own futures.

I am so grateful to Senator Feinstein for inspiring women across California and the country to run for office. I am grateful that she was a champion for women, LGBTQ rights, and gun safety legislation. Senator Feinstein’s legacy will live on for generations to come, and she will continue to inspire women across the country. My thoughts are with her family and loved ones as they mourn this tremendous loss.

In unity,

Joanna

# America’s Golden Age
---
|
---
| | |
---
| Friends, **_Our end of quarter fundraising deadline is rapidly approaching, and we are just $37,000 short of our goal._** [**Can I count on you to make our goal? Your donation of any size helps maximize our ability to send our message of American restoration to millions of Americans.**](https://larryelder.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6a42253df6197f177f9e13389&id=5c860b6a72&e=0be619cbaa) Make no mistake: this election season is just beginning. Back in 2015, Donald Trump was a longshot candidate who would go on to win the GOP nomination and the White House the following year. And unlike the candidates on that debate stage this week, I’m offering bold, America First solutions to the problems plaguing our great country. But to continue to get our message out, I need your help. I’m not a billionaire, and I’m not funded by deep pocketed special interests. I rely on the generosity of patriots like you who are willing to stand up for everyday Americans. [**So, I’m asking you to dig deep and donate whatever you can so that our America First campaign can continue to grow.**](https://larryelder.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6a42253df6197f177f9e13389&id=2fd46a645d&e=0be619cbaa) It won’t be easy, but with your prayers, generosity, and support, We the People can bring about a new American Golden Age - one that leaves behind for future generations an America even greater than we found it. Thank you,
Larry Elder
GOP Candidate for President

Hello Peter,
I'm writing to ask if you will make your first donation to our campaign to help us reach our $75,000 goal before tomorrow night's deadline. I hope you will give me a minute to explain why this request is important — **[but if you are ready to do your part right now, you can donate at this link knowing how grateful I am for your support.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20230929-4?refcode=em20230929-4&refcode2=794_552475_sDOWg1&akid=794%2E552475%2EsDOWg1)**
The truth is, defending this Senate seat isn't only about ensuring we can keep fighting for Pennsylvania families in Washington, as important as that is.
This is also the race that could decide if Democrats hold our Senate majority. We know that, and Mitch McConnell knows it, too.
It is hard to understate the stakes, Peter: Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid, women's rights, LGBTQIA+ equality, the right to vote, and more are on the line if Republicans flip the Senate next year.
We need to be able to fight back against the millions that McConnell and the GOP are going to spend here, which will hinge on our ability to meet our goals ahead of major fundraising deadlines like the one we're facing tomorrow night.
**[Can I count on you to contribute $5 or more to our re-election campaign today, Peter? I need your help to reach our end-of-quarter goal.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20230929-4?refcode=em20230929-4&refcode2=794_552475_sDOWg1&akid=794%2E552475%2EsDOWg1)**

Our deadline is less than 36 hours away and we're close to reaching our goal, so I'm hoping your donation will put us over the top.
Thank you for your support,
Bob Casey
